confirmed.repro: cd /home/nico/projects/sift-test-1; SIFT_PORT=9461 SIFT_TAB=T1-youtube bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/poll.ts 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ' 9000 R5T1-interimX. Or run scratchpad/burst.ts with the URL, a name, 3000 and 6500 to take screenshots every ~400 ms. Then look for the original's left-column title and description box at x<250 in the shots. This happened in about half of my loads.
confirmed.suspectedCause: About 3-5 s into the load the adapter goes back to the generic view, perhaps when watch() returns null or a partial page while ytd-watch-flexy settles. The switch re-renders the page, maybe re-showing the player popover, and in those frames the original page is painted over Sift's white background. Look at what changes in index.ts/portal.ts render or top-layer order between the adapter and generic views.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced in 3 of 3 fresh loads of watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ. I recorded each load as a PNG screencast and counted dark pixels in Sift's empty margins (x<250 and x 1030-1140). Each load had a run of bleed frames: 5346-5676 ms, 8937-9288 ms and 8452-8891 ms, so about 0.35-0.85 s per load, not 1-3 s. The bleed shows the original's title, channel, Subscribe, description box and Like pill, plus the related column. All of it is painted over Sift, including over the right edge of Sift's own player. One frame is a ghosted cross-fade between Sift's two layouts. Frames: /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/skv/c1/f-05346.png, c1/f-05625.png, c2/f-09153.png. The cause is not Sift's re-render. YouTube itself calls document.startViewTransition() during the watch load, which I confirmed with a main-world hook: it starts at 3.3-6.2 s, is ready about 1.2-1.8 s later and finishes about 0.4-0.9 s after that. It does this with Sift off too. The page sets view-transition-name on html (root), #player-container (player-resize), #below (metadata) and #secondary (secondary-column). The ::view-transition pseudo-tree paints above the top layer, so during the animation those named original parts are drawn over sift-root. That is why the DOM looked clean: white background, opacity 1, popovers [sift-root, div#movie_player]. The original flashes over Sift on every watch load, against the 'original never flashes' design, so high severity stands.
confirmed.fix: In src/main/index.ts (main world), wrap Document.prototype.startViewTransition. While Sift is shown, call skipTransition() on the transition it returns; the update callback still runs. Sift-shown can be read from an attribute that index.ts sets on <html> in sift mode. Another way: while in sift mode, add a page stylesheet that sets view-transition-name: none !important on the page's elements. Either way this covers every site that uses same-document view transitions, not just YouTube.

confirmed.title: Fresh watch load: keyboard focus starts in YouTube's player, and YouTube takes it back about 6 s in
confirmed.where: YouTube watch page, keyboard only, from a fresh navigation (address bar or goto)
confirmed.evidence: After a fresh load, document.activeElement is div#movie_player. The first Tab goes into YouTube's own player controls inside the portal: 13 PAGE stops ('Close' card teaser, branding button, 'Seek slider', 'fine scrubbing thumbnails' 160x0, Pause, Mute, 'Volume' 0x40, time, Autoplay, Subtitles, Settings, Theater, Full screen). Only then does Tab reach Sift's own Pause. Sift's Skip to content, Search, Menu, Sign in and Settings can't be reached by tabbing forward. Keys meant to scroll go to the player: PageDown does not scroll Sift (portal top stays 95), ArrowDown lowers the volume 0.89->0.85->0.80, Space pauses, and End seeks to the end, which with autoplay moved the tab to another video (watch?v=-OfA04BD4GA) while I was trying to scroll comments. Focus also gets taken back: in 2 of 2 runs I tabbed to Sift's Mute at 2.5 s, and by 5.9 s focus was on PAGE div#movie_player. tabwalk.ts hides all of this because it clicks inside Sift first. Shot: /home/nico/projects/sift-test-1/research/shots/R5T1-fresh-focus-in-player.png
confirmed.repro: cd /home/nico/projects/sift-test-1; SIFT_PORT=9461 SIFT_TAB=T1-youtube bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/tabs2.ts 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ' 25. It prints 'start: PAGE <div#movie_player>', then 13 PAGE stops before 'SIFT <button.btn> Pause'. For the focus being taken: SIFT_PORT=9461 SIFT_TAB=T1-youtube bun /tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/early.ts 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ'. It shows 'SIFT <button> Mute' at ~2.5-3.8 s, then 'PAGE <div#movie_player>' from ~5.9 s.
confirmed.suspectedCause: YouTube calls focus() on #movie_player when the watch page finishes loading. Sift neither moves the initial focus into its own view nor keeps focus that is already inside Sift. The portal keeps YouTube's controls tabbable even though Sift's media bar duplicates them.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced, but with a narrower scope than claimed. After a fresh load, focus starts at PAGE div#movie_player. Tab passes 13 YouTube player stops before reaching Sift's Pause. early.ts, run twice: focus was on Sift's Mute at 2.4 s, and PAGE #movie_player had it again from 5.3 s and 7.1 s. Much of this is YouTube's own behavior. With Sift off, focus also starts on #movie_player, and in 2 of 2 runs YouTube pulled focus back to #movie_player at about 6 s. On the original, ArrowDown (volume), Space (pause) and End (seek) also act on the focused player. The failure that is Sift's own is scrolling. With focus in the portal, PageDown does not scroll Sift: the portal top stays at 95 and the .sift scrollTop stays at 0. Instead it scrolls the hidden original (scrollY 0 -> 787 -> 1574). On the original, PageDown scrolls the page. So on a fresh watch load, a keyboard user cannot page through Sift's view until they tab out of 13 player controls, and YouTube's refocus at about 6 s puts them back in the player. I rate this medium, as a keyboard-accessibility gap on Sift's main YouTube page.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/index.ts, the keydown handler and onPortalKey: for scroll keys that the portal's page did not consume (PageDown and PageUp, and Space or arrows when the target is the player container itself rather than one of its controls), preventDefault and call scrollByKey() on Sift's host. Also treat focus that page script moves into a portal, with no recent pointer or key input there, as not the user's choice: keep focus on the last Sift element, or on main().

confirmed.title: Guardian article with a lead video gets no Short version, the video and its caption sit above the H1, and a 'Prefer the Guardian on Google' promo is left in
confirmed.where: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/24/israel-soldiers-raze-west-bank-neighbourhood-hebron-families-from-homes (Sift view, 1280 px)
confirmed.evidence: On 3 loads (waits of 8, 15 and 50 s), Sift's shadow root has no <article> element and no 'Show full text' toggle. The full 512-word body is shown as flat paragraphs. The order is: [PORTAL] 'Israeli troops destroy Hebron neighbourhood...' with its controls, the caption paragraph, then H1, byline 'Julian Borger · Oct 24, 2026', standfirst, a second byline 'Julian Borger in Jerusalem', an H2 collapsible 'Sat 24 Oct 2026 14.17 BST', then '[link] Prefer the Guardian on Google' (google.com/preferences/source). In the original the H1 is at y=530 and the video below it at y=708. Other Guardian articles from the same day (Lula, Meghan, France protests, which also has a lead video, Eagle's Nest, Starlink, North Korea) each get an <article class=short>, a toggle, the H1 first, and no Prefer link. Shots: /home/nico/projects/sift-test-2/research/shots/r5t2-guardian-art.png (Sift), /home/nico/projects/sift-test-2/research/shots/r5t2-guardian-art-orig.png (original, behind the consent banner); outline r5t2-guardian-art.txt.
confirmed.repro: SIFT_PORT=9462 SIFT_TAB=T2-news bun scripts/visit.ts https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/24/israel-soldiers-raze-west-bank-neighbourhood-hebron-families-from-homes gu --wait 30000, then eval document.querySelector('sift-root').shadowRoot.querySelectorAll('article').length: it gives 0. Compare with /world/2026/oct/24/lula-brazil-runoff-flavio-bolsonaro: it gives 1, with a Show full text button.
confirmed.suspectedCause: The article container is not detected on this page, so the walker renders the whole main column, including the meta aside (data-gu-name=meta, which holds the preferred-source button) and the main media before the headline. Something in this page's structure defeats the article picker in generic.ts while the other Guardian articles pass. I did not find which.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced on 2 loads (20 s and 30 s waits). Sift's shadow root has 0 <article> elements and no Show full text button. The outline order is: PORTAL video and its controls, the caption, then H1, byline, standfirst, a second byline, 'H2 Sat 24 Oct 2026 14.17 BST', then '[link] Prefer the Guardian on Google'. The Lula article has the same data-gu-name structure (media, title, headline, ..., body) and gets 1 article and a toggle. Cause, found with a page-side copy of findArticle: the body's best node climbs to <main>. The prose() climb step counts the 'More on this story' carousel (ul.carousel-small). Its li cards hold only an empty overlay <a> named by aria-label, so their headline text counts as prose and not as link text. For this short story, main prose is 4225 against 3261 for the <article> (ratio 1.30, above the 1.25 limit), so the climb goes on to main. Lula's longer body stays under 1.25. Inference: when articleEl is the root (main), articleScope returns root, and walkPage calls walk(root) on the children only, so article() never runs and no article block is emitted.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/extract/generic.ts findArticle(), in the prose() climb (~2530-2560), count an anchor's accessible name (aria-label) as link text, or skip li cards whose only link is an empty overlay anchor, so onward-story carousels do not tip the climb. Also, in extractGeneric/walkPage, when ctx.articleEl === root, route it through article() (visit the root) instead of walk(root), so a story found at the root still gets its article block and Short version.

confirmed.suspectedCause: The replayed keystrokes do not fire the key events queryly listens to for live search. Text-less onclick anchors (sort) and the icon-only close are dropped by the extractor.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced twice. After 'Buscar en todo el sitio', typing 'dolar' into the dialog's search field sets #queryly_query to 'dolar', but no results appear: the original's text has no 'Mostrando ... resultados' after 6-7 s. On the original (Sift off), real typing in the same overlay shows 'Mostrando 420609 resultados para dolar' within 5 s. In generic.ts, keep #queryly_searchfiltercontainer: the count line and the text-bearing onclick anchors with href '#' (RELEVANCIA/NUEVO) are controls and must not be dropped. Keep the overlay's close as an action when its results replace the main view.

confirmed.title: Infobae sign-in form shows English developer labels instead of the visible Spanish text
confirmed.where: https://www.infobae.com/america/ -> INICIAR SESION (Sift dialog)
confirmed.evidence: The Sift dialog reads 'keep-me-loggedin' (checkbox), 'login in' (submit button) and 'register button'. The original shows the visible texts 'Recordar', 'Ingresar' and 'REGISTRARME'. These are the site's aria-labels (input aria-label=keep-me-loggedin, button aria-label='login in', 'register button'). The same dialog uses the visible text 'Olvidé mi contraseña' for the button whose aria-label is 'forgot password'. A Spanish-speaking user sees English code-like labels on the main sign-in action. Shot: /home/nico/projects/sift-test-2/research/shots/r5t2-ib-signin.png
confirmed.repro: Open https://www.infobae.com/america/ in Sift, click INICIAR SESION, read the checkbox and button labels. Then Escape, Alt+Shift+S, click INICIAR SESION on the original: it shows Recordar / Ingresar / REGISTRARME. Do not submit.
confirmed.suspectedCause: For these controls the label is taken from aria-label before the visible text, even when the aria-label is a developer string in another language.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced. The Sift sign-in dialog shows 'keep-me-loggedin' (checkbox), 'login in' (submit) and 'register button'. The original shows Recordar / Ingresar / REGISTRARME (shot research/shots/sk-ib-signin.png). Cause in generic.ts labelOf(): for a button with an aria-label, visible text replaces the aria-label only when it has 3 or more words or 20 or more characters. So 'Olvidé mi contraseña' wins, but 'Ingresar' and 'REGISTRARME' lose to the English aria-labels. For the checkbox, accName() returns aria-label before the wrapping <label> text 'Recordar'. The original's accessible names are the same English strings (a site accessibility bug), but Sift prints them as visible text on a Spanish page, which breaks 'keeps the page's language' on the main sign-in actions.
confirmed.fix: src/content/extract/generic.ts labelOf() (~572): prefer the visible text whenever it is not contained in the aria-label (label-in-name), not only when it is 3 or more words. Do the same for inputs: when an input's aria-label looks like an identifier (hyphenated, or contains 'button'/'input') or does not contain the wrapping label's visible text, use the label text from dom.ts accName().

confirmed.suspectedCause: Two causes. Unloaded lazy images are skipped. And the Short-version figure placement puts a caption whose image was dropped at the top instead of beside its anchor paragraph.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced on 2 loads at 600x900. The Short version has 2 images (facade, interior). The Jade and Faucher captions come as plain paragraphs right after the second figure, before 'Limoges city hall was badly damaged…', away from their text. At 1280 px the same article has the Jade and Faucher images, each with its figcaption. The article key is 'art:'+refOf(el) (generic.ts article()), and a new element gives a new key. In processAi that key has no job and no store entry, so it goes through the 600 ms steady wait and a new condense. condense() only shares a job through jobs.get(src.text), an exact text match.
